echo: Customers can’t tell why we’re different, so they choose the cheaper option or a familiar name.
t1: Pick a category you can win
t2: Own it with one clear difference
p1_h1: Every time you say you’re faster, cheaper or better, you’re inviting buyers to **compare you** with cheaper options and familiar names.
p1_body: So before you change a single word of your marketing, pick a category you can *dominate*. That doesn’t mean inventing a brand-new one, because then you’d spend years educating the need for the "new category". It means finding a space buyers already understand, where far fewer businesses are competing.
was_call: The crowded category, where every agency and every alternative promises lead gen outcomes
now_call: The few agencies sitting where CRO, lifecycle email and positioning meet
story_a:
We used to call ourselves a Conversion Quiz™ agency, so buyers lumped us in with every lead gen agency out there and compared us on price. When we looked closely at how we actually work, we realised the quiz was only about 15% of it.

We aren’t a CRO agency, an email agency or a positioning agency; we sit where all three meet, a space buyers already understand but very few agencies are in. And even there, we didn’t try to be one more circle.
story_b: We led with the one thing nobody else was doing, **Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™**, so there was nothing left to compare us with.
win_s: It worked so well that I’m now writing a book on it.
next1: So how do I find what makes me different?
p2_h1: Your Contrarian POV™ is the gap only \*\*YOUR COMPANY\*\* can fill in your category.
p2_body: You don’t brainstorm your Contrarian POV™ in a creative meeting. It sits at the intersection of : what your customers struggle with, where alternatives fall short, and what you do differently to fill that gap. Here’s how we found it for a video mastermind we worked with:
cust: What they keep saying, what they’re struggling with, and what they want most.
mkt: What the alternatives are doing, and where they keep falling short.
proc: What you do differently that fills the gap the others leave behind.
case_h: The founder already had trust, with 200–300 comments on his LinkedIn posts, but he promised the same thing as every competitor, so buyers wouldn’t spend $6,000 on a claim they’d heard before.
case_bn: Booked 27 sales calls and lost 26 of them, a 3.7% close rate.
case_bs: The same promise every competitor made.
case_an: Closed the next 29 of 31 sales calls by leading with his Contrarian POV™.
case_as: Buyers kept saying “creativity” on calls, so we told them their videos don’t need high-level production; they need Creative Delivery.
case_ap: Closed 29 of 31 calls by leading with his Contrarian POV™.
cta: Show me where my buyers are finding me
up_next: Next question: Where does most of your traffic or audience come from today?
